chitchat: "Every camera is a choice the Architect made about who to watch. We make choices back."
"We don't want to burn the city down. We want the keys to it. There's a difference, and it's everything."
"Paper doesn't leak. Paper doesn't get hacked. Paper is why we're still here."
description: A tall woman with cropped iron-grey hair, standing at the great hand-drawn wall map with a grease pencil behind one ear. She has the calm of someone who plans in years, not days. When she looks at you it's not unkind, but it is complete: she is deciding what you're good for, and she is usually right.

asc_accept.text: "Green line will start you at Halcyon. Eyes open, mouth shut." She picks the pencil back up. "Come and tell me what breathes out there."

asc_after.text:
"Dig carefully. A door that opens for you out there opens for a reason, and the reason is not you."

She is already marking the western edge of the map, a shape she does not have a symbol for yet.

asc_offer.text:
"Start at the source. The claims hall in Halcyon Towers. Watch where the payouts route, and then follow the track west until it stops being grass."

A beat.

"I do not know what is out there. That is exactly why I want eyes that will come back."

options.label: There is a whole complex out there.

asc_report.text:
She listens to all of it without moving.

"A chrome city. Turrets. A Gate that turns you away."

She exhales slowly.

"So that is where the money has been going. Whatever that place is, it is the machine's friend and not ours."

A long look, and she does not soften it.

"Learn what it is, if you are going back. But Halcyon. Do not ever trust a payout from them again."

"Did anybody take your name?"

asc_reveal.text:
Cyrelle sets down the grease pencil, which is rare.

"Bothering me too. Halcyon settles its biggest claims by moving money west, past the grass, off every map we keep. Insurance does not work like that. Insurance argues. Insurance delays. Something out there is wearing Halcyon's face and it has never once argued a claim."

She studies you.

"You have earned enough rope to go and pull on it. Quietly. Find out what is west, and do not let them learn you are Watch."

blind.text:
"That is the long game. It is slow, and it is the only one worth playing."

She does not smile yet.

"Do the arithmetic before you decide you are impressed. There are sixty-one of us. On the other side there is a machine that owns every wire in the Basin, and a chrome city out west that can print a new body faster than we can bury an old one. Nobody sensible takes that bet. I want you to know that I know it."

Now the smile, and it is thin, and it is real.

"But a machine has to be told where to look. That is the one thing it has never been able to do for itself. So we do not win this with a bomb. We win it one dark corner at a time, until the map is more ours than his, and one morning it goes looking for us and finds a city with rooms of its own again."

bye.text: "Stay sharp." She turns back to the map, already somewhere else.

options.label: How long have you been sitting here?
Say what you came to say.

cross_meet.text:
She does not put a light on. She is on the stool by the type cases with her coat still buttoned, and she has clearly been there a while, and she is not surprised.

"Six nights," she says. "Halloran said four. I said seven. It was six."

She does not get up.

"Sit down. You have had a long walk and you are going to have a longer one back."

options.label: They are going to win, Cyrelle.

cross_meet2.text:
"Here is what I am not going to do. I am not going to tell you that you have made a terrible mistake, because you know, and being told is what makes a person dig in."

She nods at the press behind her.

"Take the address. Genuinely, take it. It is a machine and we have two more, and the day they come for it is the day we find out how many of them are prepared to be seen carrying a crate out of a basement."

A long pause, and she is not performing it.

"But you are still on the rota. Nobody has crossed you off. That is not sentiment. Crossing somebody off is a decision, and I am not making it while there is any version of this where you come back."

cross_open.text:
"Nothing you would have to do tonight." She says it carefully, the way you say a thing you have rehearsed and do not want to sound rehearsed.

"You would have to still be a person we could reach. That is all it is at this stage, and I am aware of exactly how much I am asking for and how little I am offering back."

She stands, finally, and pulls her coat straight.

"Go on. He will want it before morning, and you should not be the last one out of this building."

cross_refuse.text:
She takes it better than you were braced for, which is worse.

"All right."

She moves off the stool to let you past the type cases, and she is careful not to touch you doing it, and that is the part you will remember.

"For what it is worth, and it is worth nothing: I do not think you are a coward and I do not think you were bought. I think you did the arithmetic and got the right answer."

She sits back down in the dark.

"I have done it too. I just could not make myself live in it."

map.text:
"Every red mark is one of the Architect's eyes." She sweeps a hand across the east of the Basin. "Every one struck through is an eye we have closed."

"It looks like a small thing, one camera. It is not. A blind spot is a place people can breathe, and meet, and move, and a place the machine has to guess about. String enough of them together and you have something it cannot see at all."

"You have a city with rooms of its own again."

ret_accept.text:
"Then go and get her."

She marks the Vats on the wall, and for once it is not a red eye. It is a circle.

"Two rules and I am not flexible on either. You do not put a floor supervisor in the ground. Kill one of Halcyon's middle managers and by morning we did not rescue a witness, we murdered a man in a polo shirt, and every name on that slate turns into paperwork nobody will ever read. Cosh them, lock them in a cupboard, walk around them. I do not care which."

She looks up.

"And you come back at her pace. Not yours. She is carrying everything she is and she cannot run with it. If you get here without her, do not get here."

"Can you carry somebody who cannot walk?"

ret_after.text:
"Eleven thousand and forty." She says the number the way you would test a weight. "Every one of them a policy somebody's mother is still paying into. That is not a cult out there. That is a debt collector with a chapel."

She looks past you at the woman on the crate.

"She keeps the room. She keeps the name. Anybody asks, she is Watch now, and the Watch do not file people."

ret_offer.text:
"I told you the first day there would be work. Cameras to close. Its little servants to inconvenience."

She finally turns all the way round.

"And people to move out from under the machine's eye. That is the one I have never been able to hand anybody, because we have never had somebody inside worth moving."

"Now we do. And she found us."

ret_offer2.text:
"A sub-registrar in the Vats. Nine years filing the accounts they stopped paying to run."

A short breath.

"She is not a defector. She is a clerk who read her own filing cabinet and could not stop reading it. She will hand us the whole archive. She will not do it from inside that building, and she cannot get out of it on her own."

ret_report.text:
Cyrelle looks at the woman sitting on a crate in her bunker, and then at the slate, and then at the woman again, and she takes the slate second.

"Nine years." She does not say it to you. "Nine years of writing down who they were never going to bring back, and filing it, and coming in the next day."

She thumbs the archive open, reads for a while, and her face does something Halloran would not believe if you told him.

"You understand what this is. It is not proof they are a cult. Nobody cares about a cult. It is proof an insurer is selling a resurrection it has already decided not to perform."

options.label: There is more. They keep the ones who lapse.

ret_reveal.text:
She sets the grease pencil down and this time she does not pick it back up.

"Say the last part again."

You do. Cyrelle stands very still in front of a map covered in eyes she has spent her life closing.

"So the payouts were not going west to somebody. They were going west to themselves."

A flat sound that is not a laugh.

"An insurance company that owns the afterlife it is underwriting. No wonder they never argue a claim."

options.label: (she is sitting in the dark by the press)
What does the Watch actually want?
Something about Halcyon has been bothering me.
I climbed the Spire. Halcyon is them.
She is here. She is standing right there.

root.text:
She does not turn from the map at first.

"New blood. Halloran vouches for you, and Halloran is not generous with that."

Now she looks.

"I am Cyrelle. I run operations down here, which is to say I decide, most days, what the Architect gets to see next. Sit with that a moment, and then tell me what you want to know."

work.text:
"There will be operations for you soon enough. Cameras to close. People to move out from under the machine's eye. Its little servants to inconvenience."

She taps the map.

"For now, get the lie of the place. Talk to the Quartermaster. Rest while you can. When there is a run with your name on it you will hear about it."

clothing_layers: a long field coat, collar up, dead-grey

name: Cyrelle
